newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes fall, buyers assess foreigns.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes fall, buyers assess foreigns.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes, pressured by lackluster West Texas Intermediate (WTI), fell Wednesday, while refiners talked with foreign suppliers in hopes of undercutting tight discounts for Alaskan crude.
Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) remained $0.91 cents off WTI, as the grade's largest producer withheld offers for April and May barrels. Traders head no bids from refiners
Buyers preferred South American grades, with Texaco buying 400,000 barrels of Colombian South blend for May on Tuesday, and Shell reportedly taking a half million barrels of Kutubu.
Both grades resemble ANS, traders said.
A Los Angeles refinery considered Venezuelan crude, but declined to specify the grade, adding it was offered at $3.30 to 3.50 under WTI.
Others traders said the grade was Mesa.

One trader said demand for space on Line 63 could increase in May since Texaco and Unocal will return from shutdowns and Ultramar will resume buying high viscosity high sulfur crude after a month-long absense to drawdown inventory.
Outright prices for Kern River rose, with differentials firming after a supply glut abated.
Kern River, a key heavy grade, ranged $15.45/15.55 a barrel, up as discounts tightened 45 cents to hover either side of postings.
